summary: Iteration v2.3 (Notification Center + Accounting v2.3) tested end-to-end. Backend: 18/18 pytest passing. Frontend: bell (open/close/scan/read/dismiss/mark-all/link-nav) and Accounting tabs (Balance Sheet, Cash Flow) + all 5 CSV exports (pl, tb, bs, cf, journal) verified via download listener.

minor.issue: Spec says body `{status:'approved'}` but the Pydantic model (LeaveActionIn) requires `{action: 'approve'|'reject'}`. Not a bug per se, but the review-request wording diverges from the implementation — clarify in spec or add a `status` alias.
Emails are normalized to lowercase server-side. Callers must lookup pending users case-insensitively. Documented so future tests don't fail on case.

action_items: Optional: align LeaveActionIn field name to match spec (`status`) or update spec doc to say `action`.
Optional (still open from iter5): pending-user AuthContext.isRejected precedence bug — not in this iteration's scope but still to be fixed by main agent.
critical_code_review_comments: notifications.py scan endpoint is nice and idempotent via dedup_key — but it uses find_one per (user_id, dedup_key) inside emit(). For large user counts, consider a unique compound index (user_id, dedup_key) and use insert_many with ordered=False to leverage duplicate-key skip. Current O(N users) find_one is fine for the current scale.
accounting.py has grown to ~1030 lines; splitting into `accounting/reports.py`, `accounting/journal.py`, `accounting/exports.py` submodules would keep files <700 lines per guideline.

cash_flow_statement classifies inflows as 'client_payment' only when source=='invoice_payment' but the codebase never writes that source (income endpoint uses source='income'). All client payments end up as 'income'. Consider unifying or adding a doc note.
NotificationBell.jsx swallows all polling errors silently — a 401/expired-session will keep spinning quietly. Consider surfacing on repeated failures.

GET /api/notifications requires require_user (approved+active). Frontend Layout mounts NotificationBell on every route including pending screen — a pending user will just see 403s silently. Consider hiding the bell when !user.is_approved.
